description: CallCompass v2 - rebuild the demo UI around the tree as the stage, remove operator-written recommendations end to end (config, schema, API, UI), add pause/resume to recording with visible segment boundaries, and make the model's live position in the tree unmistakable. Vanilla ES modules, no build step. Full PRD at tasks/prd-callcompass-v2.md - read the relevant section verbatim rather than inventing shapes. Quality checks run from backend/: ../.venv/bin/ruff check . && ../.venv/bin/mypy callcompass && ../.venv/bin/pytest, plus node --check frontend/*.js. The only frontend test runner is pytest driving node, so any contract-bearing JS must be pure and exported from a module node can import with no DOM.

userStories.title: Remove recommendation and rationale from the tree schema, config, and API
userStories.description: As a demo operator, I want leaf nodes to be pure classification outcomes so the artifact cannot be read as giving sales advice.
acceptanceCriteria: LeafNode in backend/callcompass/tree.py no longer declares `recommendation` or `rationale`

config/tree.json has `recommendation` removed from all 16 leaf nodes, and `rationale` removed from the one leaf that carries it (out_value_reframe)
The Completed model in backend/callcompass/traversal.py no longer carries `recommendation` or `rationale`; it keeps leaf_node_id, label, path, inference_count, total_inference_ms
GET /api/tree response contains no `recommendation` or `rationale` key for any node
backend/tests/test_tree.py, test_traversal.py, test_analyze.py, test_app.py and backend/tests/fakes.py are updated for the new shapes

The assertions that currently pin recommendation/rationale rendering are removed rather than reworked: test_analyze.py's completed-payload key set, test_traversal.py's recommendation equality check, and test_frontend_analysis.py's result-card recommendation/rationale assertions

Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: PRD US-021. Backend-only and independent of every UI story, so it lands first. SCOPE REDUCED since the PRD was written: config/tree.json was already rebuilt as `northbeam-saas-v2` (26 nodes, 10 branches, 16 leaves), so the `rec_*` -> `out_*` id rename and the leaf-label rewrite are ALREADY DONE - do not redo them. What is left is the schema field removal, the Completed model, the strings in the config, and the tests. This change MUST be atomic: removing the field from LeafNode immediately breaks traversal.py's Completed construction and the config load, so schema + config + Completed + tests all move in one commit. The frontend still imports result.js at this point and will read `undefined` for the recommendation - that is expected and is fixed by US-005; do not patch result.js here. No explicit rejection logic is needed for stale configs: extra="forbid" on _Strict does it for free. Note that exactly one leaf (out_value_reframe) carries a `rationale`, deliberately, so the optional-field-present path stays covered until this story deletes the field.

userStories.title: Active-node state - where the model is right now
userStories.description: As a viewer, I want to see which node the model is currently inferring, distinct from the nodes it has already decided.
acceptanceCriteria: TreeView supports a node state data-state="active" alongside idle/visited/warning, styled with an accent ring plus a looping pulse and clearly different from visited at projector distance
Edges are never marked active - only nodes are, because only a node has an inference running on it

Analysis tracks the frontier: on `started` the root becomes active; on each `step` the stepped node flips active->visited and step.next_node_id becomes active; on `completed` the leaf flips active->visited; on `unplaced` the stopped node flips active->warning; on `error` the failing node flips active->warning
Exactly one node is active at a time while a run is in flight, and zero nodes are active before the first run and after any terminal event
TreeView.reset() clears active along with the other states
The pulse is suppressed under @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) and replaced by a static ring
backend/tests/test_frontend_analysis.py gains assertions over the frontier across a full scripted run, including the unplaced and error paths
No change is made to backend/callcompass/stream.py or the SSE event types

userStories.notes: PRD US-023, and the one genuinely non-obvious piece of v2. The backend yields a Step only AFTER that node's generate() returns, so there is no 'about to infer' frame on the wire - but the next node is fully determined: tree.root after `started`, step.next_node_id after each step. That is exactly the inference stream.py already makes internally to attribute an error to a node. Derive it client-side; do NOT add a backend event type. Highlighting must keep its existing contract of only flipping data-state and writing detail text, never re-rendering, or the ~120ms CSS transitions break.

userStories.title: Recorder pause and resume
userStories.description: As an operator, I want to pause mid-utterance and resume into the same take so I can collect my thought without starting over.
acceptanceCriteria: recorder-worklet.js accepts a {type: "paused", value: boolean} port message and stops posting sample chunks while paused, without tearing down the processor
Recorder gains pause() and resume() plus a `paused` boolean; both are no-ops when not recording and safe to call twice
Pausing keeps the MediaStream, AudioContext, worklet and analyser alive, so resume() needs no new permission prompt and adds no gap beyond the paused interval
Samples captured before and after a pause are concatenated into one buffer in order, with no silence inserted at the splice
Recorder.release() and stop() clear the paused flag, so a new start() always begins unpaused
stop() from a paused state returns the stitched recording rather than null
A node-driven test loads the worklet with globals stubbed, as the existing harness does, and asserts no chunks are posted while paused
node --check frontend/*.js passes
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: PRD US-026, and the head of a strict chain: US-011 -> US-012 -> US-013 -> US-014. Pause the worklet, not the audio graph: disconnecting nodes or suspending the AudioContext risks dropped buffers at the boundary and a visible permission/indicator flicker. A `paused` flag inside the processor, set by port message, is the minimal change - the graph keeps running and the processor simply stops posting. The browser's recording indicator stays lit while paused, which is honest, since the mic is still open. No UI in this story.

userStories.title: Segment tracking and a pause-aware clock
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the 30-second limit to count only the audio I actually recorded, and I want to know where the splices are.
acceptanceCriteria: The Recording object gains segments: Array<{startMs: number, endMs: number}> - one entry per record/resume span, as offsets into the final stitched buffer
Segment offsets are derived from accumulated sample counts, never from performance.now(), so they align exactly with the encoded WAV
A single unpaused take yields exactly one segment spanning 0 to durationMs
RecordingTimer gains pause() and resume(); elapsedMs accumulates only unpaused time and freezes while paused
The 30-second ceiling (MAX_RECORDING_MS, derived from the backend's MAX_SECONDS) applies to accumulated recorded time
The auto-stop timeout is rescheduled on resume against the remaining budget, so a paused take can neither exceed the limit nor auto-stop early
The timer readout shows a paused affordance while paused, e.g. `0:12 / 0:30 · paused`
The segment-derivation and accumulated-elapsed functions are pure and exported
backend/tests/test_frontend_timing.py is extended to cover accumulated elapsed across two pauses, the rescheduled ceiling, and segment offsets for a two-segment take
node --check frontend/*.js passes
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: PRD US-027. Depends on US-011. Wall-clock offsets drift against the resampled buffer, and a marker that does not sit on the real splice is worse than no marker - accumulate posted sample counts instead. MAX_SECONDS already comes from wav.js so the ceiling is not written out twice; keep it that way.
